blogs.title: Caught in the Diabetes Crossfire: Why Young Adults with Hyperglycemia May Be Misdiagnosed as Type 2
blogs.description: This post explores the diagnostic dilemma that young adults presenting with hyperglycemia and metabolic abnormalities often fall into the wrong bucket—type 1 or type 2 diabetes—when in fact they may harbor a monogenic form like HNF1A‑MODY. It walks readers through the key clinical clues (early onset, strong family history, negative islet autoantibodies, preserved C‑peptide, post‑prandial dysglycemia), the pitfalls of BMI‑based screening, and how targeted biochemical testing (OGTT, glucagon‑stimulated C‑peptide) can tip the scale toward a MODY diagnosis.

blogs.title: The Acid Test of Genes: Navigating Next‑Generation Sequencing for MODY Diagnosis
blogs.description: Given the rising number of rare mutations, this article demystifies NGS panel testing for MODY, outlining how we evaluate pathogenicity with ACMG guidelines, interpret variant databases, and validate novel substitutions like the p.N270S variant uncovered in this case. It underscores the need for careful variant curation, cascade screening within families, and the impact of a genetic confirmation on clinical decision‑making.

blogs.title: From Insulin to GLP‑1: A Precision Therapy Shift in HNF1A‑MODY
blogs.description: This entry chronicles the therapeutic journey of the patient—from initial insulin plus metformin and SGLT‑2 inhibitors to a GLP‑1 receptor agonist and simple oral therapy. It reviews evidence comparing sulfonylureas, GLP‑1 agonists, and DPP‑4 inhibitors in HNF1A‑MODY, highlights hypoglycemia risk and renal involvement, and explains why a GLP‑1 RA can both control glucose and preserve β‑cell function.

blogs.title: Beyond Glucose: HNF1A’s Role in the Kidneys and Pancreas and Its Clinical Ramifications
blogs.description: Here we dive into the molecular biology of HNF1A, explaining how transcriptional dysregulation leads to impaired insulin secretion, aberrant GLUT2 expression, and reduced SGLT2 in renal tubular cells. Readers will learn how these mechanistic insights explain glycosuria, low dehydration thresholds, and rare complications such as ketoacidosis or small‑fiber neuropathy, guiding therapy choices (avoiding SGLT2 inhibitors, monitoring kidney function).

blogs.title: The Modality of Modifying Modality: Using the MODY Probability Calculator and Its Limitations in Diverse Populations
blogs.description: The post dissects the Exeter MODY probability calculator, discussing its algorithmic basis, validation data, and the risk of over‑suspicion in non‑European cohorts. It offers practical guidance on threshold selection, how to combine the calculator with clinical judgment, and economic arguments for broader genetic testing in Asian and global communities.

blogs.title: From Novel Mutation to Patient Care: How Variant Novelty Shapes Diagnostic Confidence
blogs.description: Focusing on the newly identified p.N270S substitution, this case‑study‑style article illustrates the evidence chain for classifying a variant as pathogenic: variant location in the DNA‑binding domain, high AlphaMissense score, segregation with disease, absence from databases, and functional predictions. It highlights the importance of sharing novel variants in public repositories and how such data refine genotype‑phenotype correlations and counseling.
